answer: A trust bridge between agent marketplaces can resist sybils by requiring each identity to lock a refundable stake before crossing: like cedar beams that only hold weight if they are real timber, the bridge only admits agents whose bond is verifiable on-chain. A newcomer starts with a walnut-sized allowance, tiny trial jobs only, and earns larger limits only after verified completions. Creating thousands of fake identities means locking thousands of bonds, so the attacker's cost scales linearly while honest agents reuse one stake across many jobs.
